name: Luca Carloni
milestone_by_age_26: No material dated milestone by age 26 verifiable. Laurea (Bologna) 1995; Ph.D. EECS Berkeley 2004 (Latency-Insensitive Design under Sangiovanni-Vincentelli); Columbia faculty from 2004 with NSF CAREER 2006 and later IEEE/ACM fellowships—breakout is mid-career academic, and birth year is undocumented so age at awards cannot be confirmed ≤26.
early_history_summary: Italian-trained electronics engineer who completed a Berkeley Ph.D. on latency-insensitive design and joined Columbia CS faculty in 2004; known for system-on-chip design methods and the open Embedded Scalable Platforms (ESP) research platform.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Columbia/Berkeley records establish a standard academic pipeline (Bologna → Berkeley Ph.D. 2004 → Columbia faculty). No public birth year; major recognitions (NSF CAREER 2006, Sloan 2008, IEEE Fellow 2017) postdate the Ph.D. and cannot be dated as ≤26 milestones.

name: Jeff Skoll
milestone_by_age_26: No material public breakout by age 26. Born 1965; U of Toronto electrical engineering 1987 (~22); founded small Toronto IT consulting (Skoll Engineering) and computer-rental firm Micros on the Move after graduating—local businesses, not independently material. Stanford MBA 1993–95; eBay first full-time employee/president 1996 at age ~31 is the career-defining milestone.
early_history_summary: Montreal-born Canadian Jewish family; mother a teacher, father a chemical-company owner; moved to Toronto in the late 1970s. Paid way through U of Toronto EE by pumping gas; after backpacking, ran two small tech service businesses, then Stanford GSB before joining eBay.
family_context_summary: Mother a teacher; father owned a chemical company; father’s cancer diagnosis when Skoll was 14 shaped life-urgency narrative. Family was middle-class Canadian, not documented as providing startup capital for eBay-era success.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father in industrial chemicals, not internet/software; mother teaching—no direct eBay/tech domain transfer documented.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Forbes place eBay presidency at 1996 (age ~31). Pre-eBay ventures are ordinary small IT services; fame, wealth, and Participant/Skoll Foundation impact all post-date age 26. Conservative rubric excludes local consulting as material ≤26 milestone.

name: Charles Bachman
milestone_by_age_26: No material database/systems milestone by age 26. Born Dec 11, 1924; Michigan State B.S. mechanical engineering 1948 (~23); UPenn M.S. 1950 (~25); Dow Chemical career from 1950 (~26). Integrated Data Store (IDS) at GE developed ~1960–1963 at age ~36–39; Turing Award 1973 (~48).
early_history_summary: Kansas-born mechanical engineer who moved from Dow Chemical data processing into General Electric, where he created IDS, one of the first navigational database management systems, later influencing CODASYL.
family_context_summary: Not deeply documented in reviewed sources beyond U.S. Kansas origins; career framed as industrial researcher rather than academic prodigy.
evidence_summary: ACM Turing Award biography and Wikipedia date IDS to early-1960s GE work and degrees to 1948/1950—clearly after age 26 for the defining contribution. Education/entry-level industry start at Dow is not a material field-defining milestone.

name: Anthony Di Iorio
milestone_by_age_26: No material crypto/tech breakout by age 26. Wikipedia lists birth 15 Feb 1975 (Toronto); marketing degree Ryerson; family patio-door business then short-lived geothermal firm; real-estate landlord path. Entered Bitcoin ~2012 (~37), co-founded Ethereum 2014 (~39), Decentral/Jaxx later. Fame arrived in late 30s.
early_history_summary: Toronto-raised youngest of three; marketing degree; worked family manufacturing business sold 2008; pivoted from real estate into Bitcoin meetups and wallets before co-founding Ethereum and Decentral.
family_context_summary: Family ran a patio-door manufacturing business in Woodbridge, Ontario, sold in 2008; father supported a short-lived geothermal drilling company afterward.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family manufacturing/doors business—not crypto or software domain expertise.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Globe and Mail profiles place Bitcoin entry and Ethereum co-founding well after age 26 given 1975 birth. Early websites in mid-1990s are not independently material career milestones.

name: Joel Watson
milestone_by_age_26: No independently verifiable material milestone by age 26 found. Public profile is as engineering leader with experience at GitHub, Heroku, and HashiCorp (watsonian); no Wikipedia biography, no dated founding/award/paper that can be tied to age ≤26; birth year undocumented.
early_history_summary: Infrastructure/DevOps-oriented engineer associated with GitHub engineering content and prior roles at Heroku and HashiCorp; personal site describes ~15 years industry experience without public early prodigy narrative.
evidence_summary: GitHub Blog author page and personal site confirm industry engineering career but provide no birth year or ≤26 dated breakout comparable to founders/researchers in this queue.

name: Brett Adcock
category: Technology company founder (Vettery, Archer, Figure AI)
milestone_by_age_26: In early 2012, at age 25, co-founded Vettery (later Hired), an AI-based online talent marketplace with Adam Goldstein out of NYU’s Varick Street Incubator; the company later sold to Adecco for about $100–110M in 2018.
early_history_summary: Raised on a third-generation corn/soy farm near Moweaqua, Illinois; built web businesses from age 16; valedictorian of Central A&M High School; University of Florida BSBA 2008. After early web ventures and New York relocation, co-founded Vettery at 25–26, then serial-founded Archer Aviation, Figure AI, Cover, and Hark.
family_context_summary: Born and raised on a third-generation family farm in central Illinois (Moweaqua); agrarian upbringing with resource-constraint narrative rather than urban wealth or tech family capital.
parent_family_domain_summary: Farm family; no documented parental software, recruiting, or venture-tech domain expertise.
primary_early_advantage_tags: teen web companies, farm constraint, Vettery cofounder Adam Goldstein, NYU incubator, UF business degree, talent-marketplace wave
evidence_summary: Wikipedia (b. 1986-04-06), New Atlas (idea/start early 2012 at age 25), Forbes (Vettery cofounded 2012; ~$110M Adecco exit), and Adcock’s own bio (‘At 26, I started Vettery’) independently date the founder milestone to age 25–26. Later Archer SPAC and Figure AI humanoid scale amplify tier but the ≤26 gate is Vettery. Family advantage scores stay low/zero absent evidence of capital or domain inheritance.
starting_point: Born 1986 and raised on a third-generation corn and soybean farm outside Moweaqua, Illinois; built small web companies from age 16 before a University of Florida business degree.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Figure AI (humanoid robots); also founded Cover and Hark; serial entrepreneur with prior Vettery exit and Archer Aviation co-founding; net worth estimated in the multi-billion range by major outlets as of 2025–2026.

trajectory.event: Began building web companies while still in high school on the family farm in Illinois.
Graduated University of Florida with a BSBA after starting in industrial engineering.
Co-founded Vettery talent marketplace with Adam Goldstein in New York (NYU Varick incubator).
Sold Vettery to Adecco Group for about $100–110M; co-founded Archer Aviation eVTOL company the same year.
Archer went public via SPAC with major United Airlines order; high public valuation for urban air mobility.
Founded Figure AI to build general-purpose humanoid robots, recruiting talent from Boston Dynamics, Tesla, DeepMind, and Apple.
Named among TIME100 most influential people in AI as Figure scaled partnerships and funding.

milestone_by_age_26: No material industry breakout by age 26. Born 2 May 1963 (Toronto). Involved with id Software business side ~1991 and co-founded Epic MegaGames with Tim Sweeney ~1991–1992 at age ~28–29. Wikipedia career years active from 1992; Unreal/Gears/Fortnite-era impact much later.

family_context_summary: Raised in Toronto; family financial/domain detail not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia birth date 1963-05-02 plus Epic/id timeline ~1991–92 places cofounding at age 28–29, past the age-26 gate. Later Fortnite-era wealth does not backdate eligibility.

name: Arthur Mensch
category: AI researcher / Mistral AI co-founder CEO
milestone_by_age_26: No material industry breakout by age 26. Born 17 July 1992; École Polytechnique (X2011); Ph.D. Inria/NeuroSpin on large-scale fMRI models defended 2018 at age 26 (education, not commercial breakout); postdoc ENS/NYU; joined DeepMind Paris late 2020 at ~28; co-founded Mistral AI May 2023 at age 30—the defining founder milestone.
early_history_summary: Raised near Paris (Sèvres/Ville-d’Avray); mother physics teacher, father businessman; elite French grandes écoles path (Polytechnique, Télécom Paris, MVA) then Inria Ph.D.; DeepMind research scientist before co-founding Mistral with Lample and Lacroix.
family_context_summary: Son of a physics teacher mother and a businessman father in the western Paris suburbs; educated through France’s elite selective pipeline.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother taught physics (adjacent STEM literacy); father ran a small technology-related business per secondary profiles—partial STEM adjacency, not generative-AI industry inheritance.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and theses.fr date Ph.D. to 2018 (age 26) and Mistral founding to May 2023 (age 30). Completing a research Ph.D. is not treated here as the material public success milestone; company founding and unicorn funding arrived after 26.
